commands: Inspect ClusterDecoration#drawU, USymbolRectangle#asBig, and PackageStyle#toUSymbol at Java revision 71806a23780b04a5ccde2f8ceb5121edad5eb711

supported: ClusterDecoration#drawU obtains the USymbol.asBig TextBlock and draws it after applying rectangleArea.getPosition(), so border and title share one translated local origin.
USymbolRectangle#asBig draws URectangle at local origin and draws the title at local y = 2 + dimStereo.getHeight(); with an empty stereotype this is the rectangle's shared title baseline.
PackageStyle#toUSymbol maps RECTANGLE to USymbols.RECTANGLE, so a plain packageStyle rectangle is a valid sibling of an explicit Rectangle symbol.

The correction commit changes only emit_layout_rectangle_cluster's title y expression from cluster.y + PACKAGE_TITLE_BASELINE + 1.0 to y + PACKAGE_TITLE_BASELINE; it introduces no new constant or fixture branch.
implementation_audit: No production reference to class-rectangle-cluster-title-origin, checker3 names, checker2 names, RectangleOwnerEast, golden paths, fixture embedding, or coordinate-keyed SVG surgery was found.
No new unexplained numeric constant was introduced by dc0aee28. PACKAGE_TITLE_BASELINE is pre-existing and the correction removes a trailing one-pixel literal.

Rust skinparam.rs stores packageStyle in Theme.package.style, but the class renderer search found no consumer that maps that value to a package render kind. Rust package shape selection in class.rs uses package kind and explicit stereotypes; it does not reproduce Java's plain packageStyle rectangle fallback.
The three predecessor rejected rectangle counterexamples are now structurally equivalent with the corrected detached binary.

findings.summary: Plain packageStyle rectangle is not modeled by the Rust class renderer.
findings.evidence: Java PackageStyle.toUSymbol maps RECTANGLE to USymbols.RECTANGLE and therefore uses the same USymbolRectangle.asBig origin rule for plain packages. Four fresh valid inputs across TB/LR, top-level/nested, short/long labels, and competing owners instead produce Rust folder-style paths. The direct TB and LR controls show Java rectangle titles at y=22.5352 while Rust's folder titles are at y=21.5352, with different primitive sequences and layout envelopes.

findings.summary: Three explicit nested or competing-owner cases still have a 10px envelope-width mismatch.
findings.evidence: checker3_tb_competing_frame_node_rootlinks, checker3_tb_competing_nested_rectangle, and checker3_tb_stereo_nested_long fail only on the outer SVG width. Their rectangle primitive and title coordinates match the Java output; this review does not attribute those failures to the title-origin correction, but preserves them as executable residue.

findings.summary: The one-line explicit rectangle correction itself is supported where its renderer is reached.
findings.evidence: Four fresh direct explicit-rectangle cases and all three preserved predecessor counterexamples are structurally equivalent. No fixture-shaped production logic or unexplained constant was found in the exact correction diff.

rejection_basis: Fresh valid plain-title siblings fail across both directions and top-level/nested contexts because packageStyle rectangle fallback is absent from Rust. This is mechanism-relevant to the requested plain/stereotyped title generalization even though the explicit-symbol one-pixel correction passes its direct controls.
